title: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics workflows in cancer research: the relevance of choosing the right steps. Mass Spec Methods
projectDescription: The qualitative and quantitative description of proteome changes that condition cancer development can be achieved by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). LC-MS-based proteomics strategies are carried out according to predesigned workflows that comprise of several steps such as sample selection, sample processing including labelling, MS acquisition methods, statistical treatment and bioinformatics to understand the biological meaning of the findings and set predictive classifiers. As the choice of best options might not be straightforward, we will herein review and assess past and current proteomics approaches for the discovery of new cancer biomarkers. While some aspects of the workflows might be subjected to sample type and size, we recommend, based on our experience and on others, the use of bead-based sample preparation followed by data-independent acquisition (DIA) with label-free quantification methodologies or data-dependent acquisition (DDA) with tandem mass tags (TMT) quantification for broad proteome and phosphoproteome characterizations. Moreover, we will review major bioinformatics tools to interpret and visualize proteomics results and suggest most popular machine learning techniques for the selection of predictive biomarkers. Finally, we would like the reader of this manuscript to reflect on the approximation of proteomics strategies to clinical diagnosis and prognosis by discussing current barriers and proposals to circumvent them
sampleProcessingProtocol: MS methods tests were carried out with HeLa peptides from cell lysates prepared with SDS-based lysis buffer and processed with the SP3 procedure with trypsin. Phosphopeptide enrichment was performed with MagReSyn Ti-IMAC HP beads (Resyn Biosciences, Gauteng, South Africa). Only TMT-labeled peptides and phosphopeptides were fractionated by offline high pH reversed-phase chromatography.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files were analyzed using Proteome Discoverer (PD) or Spectronaut for DDA and TMT or DIA data, respectively (see next section). Spectral libraries were created in Spectronaut joining fractionated DDA and DIA data. We filtered the proteomics data for high FDR and contaminants. The phosphopeptides were filtrated by FDR, contaminants and those that contains at least one phospho-group.
keywords: Mass spectrometry; proteomics; sample preparation; data-dependent acquisition (dda); data-independent acquisition (dia); workflows
